correctness.rationale: All width-two rooted forests are one chain, two chains, or one two-arm fork with unary stem. Direct ideal covers yield explicit mutually distinguishable bivariate polynomials; coefficients solve stem and arm sums/products. Univariate specialization gives exact fibre cardinalities; coprime divisor algebra gives the stem-one odd factor criterion. Independent direct bitmask enumeration verifies 323 classes up to size 15, with no extrapolation needed for the proof.

value.rationale: Complete all-order resolution of a natural local counting invariant on every finite rooted-forest ideal lattice of width at most two, with closed-form one-sided fibre multiplicities and sharp first failures at five/six vertices. The odd-factorization criterion produces an infinite, arithmetic collision spectrum. The class is intrinsically defined by width two, and paired versus one-sided counting reflects a substantive logical-information boundary.
